findings.source_passage: the Pequod, freighted with savages, and laden with fire, and burning a corpse, and plunging into that blackness of darkness, seemed the material counterpart of her monomaniac commander's soul
findings.source_locator: climactic paragraph of the night-watch description
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves this sentence but drops the preceding clause 'as the wind howled on, and the sea leaped, and the ship groaned and dived' only partially — crucially it omits 'scornfully champed the white bone in her mouth, and viciously spat round her on all sides' from the anaphoric buildup. Wait — actually those are present. But the draft omits the key phrase 'and scornfully champed the white bone in her mouth' — let me recheck: the draft does include it. On closer inspection, the draft also omits 'as to and fro, in their front, the harpooneers wildly gesticulated with their huge pronged forks and dippers' — 'and dippers' is dropped. Minor, not critical.
findings.suggested_fix: This is not a meaningful loss; disregard.

findings.source_passage: A stark, bewildered feeling, as of death, came over me. Convulsively my hands grasped the tiller, but with the crazy conceit that the tiller was, somehow, in some enchanted way, inverted. My God! what is the matter with me?
findings.source_locator: paragraph describing the disorientation at the helm
findings.why_it_matters: The draft compresses 'A stark, bewildered feeling, as of death, came over me' and entirely omits the exclamatory 'My God! what is the matter with me? thought I' — this interior voice-cry is a key register-establishing moment of Ishmael's self-consciousness and panic; the draft replaces the whole sequence with a flat summary ('I felt something fatally wrong').
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'A stark, bewildered feeling, as of death, came over me' and 'My God! what is the matter with me? thought I' to preserve Ishmael's first-person panic and the chapter's introspective pivot.

findings.source_passage: Would that he consumed his own smoke! for his smoke is horrible to inhale... It smells like the left wing of the day of judgment; it is an argument for the pit.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves these lines well verbatim — no loss here. Disregard.

findings.source_passage: It was in the left hand try-pot of the Pequod, with the soapstone diligently circling round me, that I was first indirectly struck by the remarkable fact, that in geometry all bodies gliding along the cycloid, my soapstone for example, will descend from any point in precisely the same time.
findings.source_locator: paragraph describing the try-pots' uses, near end
findings.why_it_matters: This is a characteristically Melvillean digression — wry, absurdist, intellectually playful — and is entirely absent from the draft. It establishes Ishmael's voice as curious and comic even amid industrial description, and critics note it as a signature tonal marker.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the cycloid observation, even in abbreviated form: 'It was in the left-hand try-pot of the Pequod that I was first struck by the geometric fact that all bodies gliding the cycloid descend from any point in precisely the same time.'

findings.source_passage: Uppermost was the impression, that whatever swift, rushing thing I stood on was not so much bound to any haven ahead as rushing from all havens astern.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft reduces this to 'Uppermost, that what I stood on rushed from all havens astern' — losing the careful syntactic shape and the phrase 'whatever swift, rushing thing I stood on was not so much bound to any haven ahead as,' which is essential to the passage's rhetorical force.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'whatever swift, rushing thing I stood on was not so much bound to any haven ahead as rushing from all havens astern' verbatim.

findings.source_passage: the man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain (i.e., even while living) in the congregation of the dead
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves this but drops the italics/em notation signaling biblical quotation format. Minor but affects scholarly texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain the italicized formatting of the Solomon quotation as in the source.

summary: The draft's most serious failure is the complete omission of the cycloid/try-pot digression — a signature Ishmael voice-establishing passage — and significant compression/paraphrasing of the disorientation sequence that loses Melville's first-person exclamatory panic ('My God! what is the matter with me?'), together constituting sufficient medium-severity findings to require regeneration.
